}}'''Khamnigan''' (Khamnigan: {{MongolUnicode|ᠬᠠᠮᠨᠢᠭᠠᠨ|lang=ykh}}) is a [[Mongolic language]] spoken by the [[Hamnigan]] people east of [[Lake Baikal]].

== Usage ==
The [[Hamnigan|Khamnigan people]], called the ''Horse [[Tungusic peoples|Tungus]]'' or ''Steppe Tungus'', are natively bilingual, speaking both a Mongolic and a [[Tungusic languages|Tungusic]] language, which are inherited from their mixed ancestry. This bilingualism appears to be several centuries old. Their Tungusic language is [[Evenki language|Evenki]] (''Khamnigan'' is the Mongol name for the Evenki), while Khamnigan Mongol is a distinct Mongolic language, not a dialect of Mongol or Buryat as traditionally classified in Mongolia or in Russia. Mongol is the dominant language; the two dialects of Evenki are only used by part of the population, and only within the home.

Use of the language has declined in Russia, with few speakers left, but both Khamnigan Mongol and Evenki bilingualism remain vigorous in China. Khamnigan Evenki, though not a distinct language from other Evenki, is heavily influenced by Mongol, especially in vocabulary. Khamnigan Mongol, on the other hand, is the most conservative Mongolic language, little different from [[Middle Mongolian]], though the system of [[vowel harmony]] has been disrupted. There is little influence from Evenki: although Khamnigan Evenki has a grammatical plural, for example, Khamnigan Mongol does not.<ref>[[Juha Janhunen]]. 2003. "Khamnigan Mongol". In ''The Mongolic Languages''</ref>

Khamnigan in Mongolia has strongly assimilated to Khalkha Mongolian, and even though some Buryat-like and idiosyncratic features are to be found (e.g. the very particular mood system lacking in Khamnigan in China), it overall resembles a dialect of Khalkha, and it has lost its particular Tungusic lexicon.<ref>cf. Yu, Wonsoo. 2011. A Study of the Mongol Khamnigan spoken in Northeastern Mongolia. Seoul: Seoul National University Press.</ref>

== Orthography ==
{{Expand section|date=May 2024}}
Khamnigan is written using the [[Mongolian script]].{{cn|date=March 2026}}. In Russia, Khamnigan is written using [[Cyrillic]] (Russian alphabet with additional letters Ө ө and Ү ү).<ref>{{cite news|title=В Забайкальском крае составят алфавит хамниганского языка|url=https://nazaccent.ru/content/43136-v-zabajkalskom-krae-sostavyat-alfavit-hamniganskogo-yazyka/|accessdate=2024-11-20|publisher=Национальный акцент|date=2024-11-15|language=ru}}</ref>
